texts: Storms come over the Cold Sea in autumn and early winter.
The autumn equinox begins the storm season.
Autumn storms sometimes destroy Cliff Path lanterns.
The fishing fleet stays near the harbor in winter.
The fleet sails far in summer.
The fleet's safe return depends on the harbor wall lanterns.
A bad winter for lanterns is a bad winter for fishing.

fields.sentence: Storms come over the Cold Sea in autumn and early winter.
parse: (: storms_come (Implication (Member $x storm) (And (Member (sk_come $x) come) (Patient (sk_come $x) $x) (Over (sk_come $x) cold_sea) (Or (Time (sk_come $x) autumn) (Time (sk_come $x) early_winter)))) (STV 0.9 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: The coordination 'in autumn and early winter' is encoded as (Or (Time ... autumn) (Time ... early_winter)), but the text says 'and' — the Disjunction section applies only to surface 'or', and because Or is opaque and never asserts a disjunct, both time claims become unqueryable instead of the two conjoined Time facts the distributive coordination rule requires.

q2_gaps: modified / partial season expressions ('early winter', 'late summer') have no licensed Time term — the structured terms are Year/Month/Day/Weekday/Hour/Minute, day-parts are bare symbols, and only speech-anchored deictics ('last_spring', 'next_summer') form compound season constants, so a non-deictic 'early winter' has no defined encoding
a bare non-deictic season name ('in autumn') is not explicitly licensed as a bare Time filler either — it is neither a listed structured term nor a deictic constant
review.notes: 'the Cold Sea' is handled exactly per the Kestrel River pattern (one name symbol + Name + separate kind atom), the Patient role for the non-volitional natural-force subject 'storms' is correct, and (Over ...) is the licensed preposition-named oblique. The rule strength 0.9 says an arbitrary storm comes over this one named sea, which reads high for the striking-verbal-generic base-rate check.

issues.reason: Encoding a surface "and" with the opaque Or head is unlicensed — Disjunction is keyed to surface "or", and the doctrine bars Or even there when both members are asserted ("fell 12 tons, or 8 percent" is two true MeasureBy atoms, never an Or) — so the parse records an uncertainty the text does not state and puts both stated season facts behind an opaque head where nothing binds them.

gaps_confirmed: a modified / partial season expression ("early winter") has no licensed Time filler: the structured terms are Year/Month/Day/Weekday/Hour/Minute, day-parts are bare symbols, only speech-anchored deictics form compound season constants, and the compound-concept machinery does not reach time constants, so early_winter is an unlicensed coinage
new_gaps: distributive coordination inside a Skolem-function generic rule has no licensed shape: per-conjunct replication needs two distinct per-storm events, but a Skolem event term is a function of the bound variable and the verb only ((sk_come $x)), so two rules — or two Time atoms in one conclusion — collide on one event and assert a single storm-coming in both seasons; a seasonal-occurrence claim over a kind ("storms come in autumn and early winter") therefore has no licensed carrier at all
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form would assert both seasons as ordinary conjoined content instead of hiding them behind Or, but the instruction set licenses no way to do that here — two Time atoms on the single (sk_come $x) event would claim one storm-coming happening in both autumn and early winter, and per-conjunct replication cannot mint two distinct per-binding events — so no compliant form exists for this sentence and the construction is filed as a gap.
adjudication.notes: Everything else conforms: the Cold Sea takes the Kestrel River name+kind pattern, Patient is right for a non-volitional natural force, and (Over ...) is the licensed preposition-named oblique. I do not confirm the reviewer's second gap — "a deictic or named time stays a bare symbol" reasonably covers a bare season name on Time.

fields.sentence: The autumn equinox begins the storm season.

review.notes: Both compounds fuse correctly with head genus only (the noun modifiers `autumn` and `storm` are rightly not exposed), the inanimate transitive subject takes `Agent`, definite singulars get witnesses, and the bare present correctly gets no status atom. `Patient` on 'the storm season' follows the occurrence-object rule, though the Inception section gives a begun activity `Theme` plus `Ongoing` -- the boundary for `begin` with an event-denoting NP object rather than a to-V complement is not settled in the text.

fields.sentence: Autumn storms sometimes destroy Cliff Path lanterns.

q1_issues.issue: The bare-plural object 'Cliff Path lanterns' is rendered as a single Skolem witness ((Member (sk_lantern $x) lantern)), silently singularizing it — a plural set taking part in the occurrence is specified to take a group witness, not one individual.

q2_gaps: an unnumbered bare-plural OBJECT inside a distributing rule's conclusion — the instruction set specifies group-witness vs bare-kind-filler only for episodic clauses, and Skolem groups only for a stated number under a universal, so nothing states which form a plural object takes in a generic rule
review.notes: Otherwise correct: autumn_storm genus without a noun-modifier genus, the Northgate-spokesman Possession route for the proper-noun premodifier with (Member cliff_path path) and no name decomposition, the 'sometimes' 0.5 strength with its mandatory QuantifierPhrase companion, and no tense atom on the habitual.

issues.reason: The group-witness requirement the issue cites is stated for a bare plural in an EPISODIC clause ('rescuers reached the ridge' / 'crates were stacked with melons'), a section that expressly hands genuinely generic clauses to the rule route instead, and every atom the parser emitted inside that rule — a per-storm destroy event whose Patient is a lantern possessed by cliff_path — is true of the sentence and well-typed, so this is licensed improvisation in exactly the coverage gap the reviewer itself names rather than a false, ill-typed or over-asserted atom.

gaps_confirmed: no stated form for an unnumbered bare-plural OBJECT inside a generic rule's conclusion: the group-witness vs bare-kind-filler split is fixed only for episodic clauses, the DEPENDENT-existential example is singular ((sk_book $x)), and the per-binding Skolem GROUP is given only for a stated number under a universal ((sk_books $x) + Cardinality), leaving the plural-without-count case unspecified
adjudication.notes: Also checked and sound: the proper-noun-premodifier route (head parsed normally + opaque Possession to cliff_path, head noun kept out of the Name string), (Member cliff_path path) licensed by the kind word inside the name, no modifier genus on the name, the autumn_storm genus with the noun modifier unexposed, and 'sometimes' at strength 0.5 with its mandatory QuantifierPhrase companion and no tense atom. The distributing-rule route rather than a kind-level relation is defensible here because the Cliff Path restriction on the object has no slot in an opaque two-kind relation, mirroring the 'stray dogs chase cyclists' note.

fields.sentence: The fishing fleet stays near the harbor in winter.

q1_issues.issue: "near the harbor" is stored as (Location sk_stay_1 sk_harbor_1), collapsing a proximity relation into the in/at/on Location role and asserting the staying was at the harbor, where a non-containment position preposition is supposed to keep its surface head (the same open licence that gives "next to the kiln" its NextTo).

review.notes: The rest follows the instruction set: the time modifier "in winter" is a licensed reification trigger for a stay/remain position clause, the stative-intransitive subject correctly takes Experiencer, the habitual present correctly takes no status atom, and fishing_fleet carries its head genus with no noun-modifier genus.

issues.reason: Where a THING is licenses exactly this shape for a position clause that a reification trigger anchors — "Reify the postural state — Experiencer subject + Location oblique" — and its own illustration of that trigger ("was lying across the threshold") carries a non-containment preposition, so the surface-head rule the reviewer cites governs the un-reified entity-attached case (LocatedIn is containment ONLY) and not the reified state's oblique.

new_gaps: Proximity preposition on a REIFIED position state ("stays near the harbor in winter"): the Where a THING is recipe names the Location oblique for the reified case while the un-reified counterpart demands the surface head for every non-containment preposition (NextTo, Against, Atop), and the word "near" appears nowhere in the instruction set — so (Location e harbor) vs (Near e harbor) is underdetermined, and the two say different things about whether the staying is AT the harbor.
adjudication.notes: The rest checks out: "stay + locative PP" is routed to Where a THING is by the Resultatives cross-reference, "in winter" is a listed reification trigger, the collective noun "the fishing fleet" takes a plain witness with no GroupOf, and fishing_fleet exposes only its head genus.

fields.sentence: The fleet sails far in summer.

q2_gaps: the spatial-extent adverb "far" on a motion verb ("sails far") has no licensed slot -- it is not a *how*-adverb so `Manner` is barred, `Degree` takes an entity plus an adjective/quantity scale rather than an event, and `Measure` needs a magnitude and unit; the instruction set's adverb rule says to leave it out and record the gap, which the parse does
review.notes: Everything emitted is correct: the singular collective noun "the fleet" is one participant with no `GroupOf` and no distribution rule, a vessel under its own power keeps `Agent`, the bare simple present correctly gets no status atom (habitual default), and the season rides `Time` as a bare constant with no `Every` since no "every" wording is present. The only loss is the unencodable "far".

fields.sentence: The fleet's safe return depends on the harbor wall lanterns.

q1_issues.issue: The nominalized "safe return" is asserted at top level as an occurring event (statements 1-3 at strength 1.0), although the sentence only makes that return contingent on the lanterns and never claims the fleet returned safely.

q2_gaps: an event nominalization whose occurrence is NOT asserted - here the subject of "depends on" - has no non-asserting carrier: the noun-argument rules reify such a nominalization and give its genitive a subject role, but nothing licenses reifying it without thereby asserting that the eventuality occurred (compare the irrealis-clause gap, where the instruction is to leave the clause unencoded)
review.notes: The genitive-subject routing (Agent on the return, a self-powered vessel mover), the incidental-description split for "safe", and the prepositional-verb oblique (On) are all correct per the instruction set. "Harbor wall lanterns" is fused as a classifier compound rather than split into lanterns PartOf a harbor wall - borderline, but defensible under the classifier reading.

issues.reason: The reified return carries no tense or status atom, and the instruction set makes exactly that form occurrence-neutral — Status predicates: an event with no status predicate is "not a specific occurrence"; a reified non-finite complement with no status "asserts or denies nothing about occurrence"; and a temporal-anchor event noun ("before the inspection") gets its class atom and nothing else precisely so no occurrence is claimed — so the three return atoms do not assert that the fleet returned safely.

adjudication.notes: The reviewer's q2 gap is not a gap: the non-asserting carrier is the untensed reification itself, which the noun-argument rules already prescribe (a genitive naming an event noun's underlying subject takes that subject role). The (On sk_depend_1 ...) oblique is the instruction set's own "depend on the pump" case, and Experiencer on the stative intransitive subject follows the intransitive-subject test.

fields.sentence: A bad winter for lanterns is a bad winter for fishing.

q2_gaps: a copular generic whose subject and predicate are both restricted kinds sharing one head noun ("A bad winter for X is a bad winter for Y") — Categorical statements would give a single Inheritance between the two complex kinds, while the relational-universal-with-copular-conclusion precedent gives the restriction-in-premises Implication used here; nothing in the instruction set selects between them

the adjective+PP-complement fusion rule ("sensitive_to_light") is stated for a PREDICATIVE kind-level generic; its use here is attributive, inside the NP "a bad winter for lanterns", which the instruction set does not address
review.notes: The fused properties bad_for_lanterns / bad_for_fishing carry the correct genus + argument decomposition, "fishing" is correctly left underived, and 0.9/0.9 is the right empirical-generic dial. The only open question is the choice of rule form over a flat Inheritance, which the instruction set leaves under-determined.
